01.title: Dalua.top
01.description: Full online store for a hair care brand: catalog, customer accounts, cart, Mercado Pago checkout, shipping quotes from Melhor Envio, and an admin panel where the owner manages products, orders, coupons and content.
01.challenge: The brand needed to sell and ship without a developer in the loop, on a hosting plan it already paid for that only offered MySQL with no external access and could not build the project.
decisions: Database moved from Postgres to MySQL with Drizzle, with migrations applied automatically on server boot, since the host offers no shell and no external database connection.
Builds run in GitHub Actions with standalone output and are published to a deploy branch, because the host's build server cannot run next build.

Mercado Pago and Melhor Envio are connected over OAuth2 by the store owner, with tokens encrypted with AES-256-GCM and refreshed inside a row-locked transaction, since the refresh token is single-use.
Admin panel for banners, FAQ, coupons and shipping rules (markup, handling time, free shipping), with images converted to WebP on the server and testimonial videos converted in the browser.

02.title: Collaborative Text Editor
02.description: A simplified Google Docs style editor built on the MERN stack, with rich text, autosave, guest mode, and documents modeled as a CRDT so concurrent edits merge without conflicts.
02.challenge: Letting several people edit the same document without losing anything. The product is deliberately simple so the effort goes into sync and persistence engineering.
decisions: Documents are modeled as a CRDT with Yjs: the server receives binary updates over Socket.io and merges them before persisting to MongoDB, so concurrent edits converge without locks or last-write-wins.
Guest mode: anyone can start writing without signing up, their documents move to the account once they register, and a job cleans up abandoned guests.
Authentication with Better Auth on MongoDB, with email verification through Resend.
Monorepo with separate CI for web and server on GitHub Actions, and a release that only ships when both pass: server on Fly.io, web on Vercel.

03.title: Higher Up Business English
03.description: Website for the only company in Brazil using the BELF methodology (Business English as a Lingua Franca), with clients in Europe, the US and Japan, and pages per solution and audience in Portuguese and English.
03.challenge: A business English school for executives needed an online presence that matched its audience, was easy to find on Google, and turned visits into leads.
decisions: Next.js with pages per solution (companies, professionals, startups, teachers) and events, so each audience lands on a page written for them.
Bilingual with next-intl and locale-based routes, plus metadata, sitemap and robots generated by the app for SEO.
Umami for analytics: it measures visits without cookies, so the site needs no consent banner.
Deployed on Vercel behind Cloudflare and optimized to load in about 1 second worldwide, since the clients are spread across Europe, the US and Japan.

bullets: Designed the architecture of a multi-tenant scheduling platform as the primary developer (Java, Spring Boot, Hibernate, PostgreSQL, Flyway).

Ran a spike comparing database-per-tenant, schema-per-tenant and shared-schema strategies, and implemented schema-per-tenant isolation with Hibernate's CurrentTenantIdentifierResolver and MultiTenantConnectionProvider, keeping client data isolated on a single database.
Wrote integration tests that run CRUD operations against every table to validate manually provisioned tenant schemas before they go live.

Built automatic provider fallback for casino game integrations during the migration required by Brazil's 2024 betting regulation: when a provider was offline, requests were routed to the next available one, keeping games online. Also built a feature to manage providers dynamically.
Built a referral system end to end (Python + Next.js) in a two-person team, which drove around 10% revenue growth.
Monitored and validated platform features overnight during the migration of billions of records from the EU to Brazil.

Built and maintained daily automation jobs integrating 3 databases (PostgreSQL, SQL Server) with Lecom (BPM platform), DocuSign and Feedz (HR platform) via REST APIs, cutting one process from 4 days to 2 hours.

Built an asset management system (NestJS + Next.js) from scratch for an 8-person team, replacing two spreadsheets for tracking and history across 300+ assets; reports that took 2–3 days of manual consolidation now generate in under a minute.
Introduced unit and integration tests with Jest after repeated regressions whenever Lecom workflows were updated.
Joined an AB InBev project as the only fullstack developer on a 6-person team running a month behind schedule; delivered React + Express.js features that brought it back on track within a month.

Built, solo in 2 weeks, a pipeline importing millions of Excel rows into a relational database for a US manufacturing client, using AWS SQS for asynchronous batch processing so the API stayed responsive.
Deployed new microservices to Kubernetes and configured their networking alongside the tech lead.
Started as the only React Native developer in a 5-person company and moved to fullstack within a month.
Built a mobile inventory feature with QR code scanning and voice recognition for a large wholesale distributor, replacing manual stock counts.
Built a damage reporting system (React + Spring Boot on AWS) letting warehouse teams track incoming shipments and log damaged products with photos.
Set up the company's first CI/CD pipeline with Jenkins.
